name: Achim
overview: Achim was a male descendant from the tribe of Judah, recognized primarily as the son of Zadok within the genealogy of the Messiah. His role is noted in the New Testament as part of the lineage leading to Jesus Christ, highlighting his place in the fulfillment of God's redemptive plan. There are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Achim means 'he establishes,' reflecting a possible theme of foundation or confirmation. This proper name is not indicated to be given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful Hebrew significance. Achim is mentioned specifically in Matthew 1:14.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Achim was the son of Zadok and the father of Eliud, as stated in Matthew 1:14. These relationships place him firmly within the ancestral line leading to Christ. No other family relationships are documented beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Achim's significance lies in his position within the Messianic genealogy presented in Matthew 1:14, connecting the Old Testament promises to their fulfillment in Jesus Christ. As a member of the tribe of Judah, he represents the continuation of God's covenantal promises through David's line. His presence in the lineage underscores the historical reality and divine orchestration behind the birth of the Savior.
